first-aid-kit.definition: A portable collection of supplies for first aid.
first-aid-kit.exampleUsage: The trainer opens the first aid kit on the table.

bandage.definition: A strip or piece of material used to cover or support an injured body part.
bandage.exampleUsage: The bandage roll stays in the training box.

gauze.definition: A loosely woven fabric used in medical dressings.

adhesive-tape.definition: A thin strip with a sticky surface, used to attach or secure things.
adhesive-tape.exampleUsage: The trainer puts adhesive tape beside the gauze.

antiseptic-wipe.definition: A disposable wipe containing an antiseptic solution for cleaning intact skin or, when labeled for it, small areas around minor injuries.
antiseptic-wipe.exampleUsage: The first-aid cabinet contained individually wrapped antiseptic wipes.

scissors.definition: A cutting tool with two blades joined at a pivot.
scissors.exampleUsage: The trainer keeps the scissors closed on the table.

tweezers.definition: A small tool consisting of two pointed arms used for picking up small objects or plucking hairs.
tweezers.exampleUsage: Omar examines the tweezers, a small tool with two narrow arms.

safety-pin.definition: A metal pin with a spring and a guard that covers its sharp point when closed.
safety-pin.exampleUsage: The closed safety pin is on the training tray.

elastic-bandage.definition: A stretchable bandage used as a medical support or covering.
elastic-bandage.exampleUsage: The elastic bandage is rolled inside the kit.

triangular-bandage.definition: A triangular piece of cloth used as a bandage or sling.
triangular-bandage.exampleUsage: The trainer unfolds a triangular bandage to show its shape.

gauze-pad.definition: A sterile or clean absorbent square of woven material used to cover or cushion a wound.
gauze-pad.exampleUsage: The first-aid kit included sealed gauze pads.

burn-cream.definition: A topical product labeled for certain minor burns; more serious burns require professional medical assessment.
burn-cream.exampleUsage: The first-aid supplies included a burn cream for minor injuries as directed on the label.

cold-pack.definition: A pack designed to become or remain cold for temporary application to an injury or swollen area.
cold-pack.exampleUsage: The first-aid room stores cold packs for supervised use.

heat-pack.definition: A pack designed to provide controlled warmth for temporary application to the body.
heat-pack.exampleUsage: The heat pack was kept with other first-aid supplies.

finger-splint.definition: A rigid or semi-rigid support used to limit movement of an injured finger until appropriate medical assessment.
finger-splint.exampleUsage: The first-aid kit contained finger splints for trained responders.

medical-tape.definition: Adhesive tape designed for securing dressings or medical materials to skin.
medical-tape.exampleUsage: Medical tape was stored beside the dressings.

antibiotic-ointment.definition: A topical medicine containing an antibiotic for certain minor skin infections or wounds; it should be used only according to professional or label guidance.
antibiotic-ointment.exampleUsage: The cabinet stored antibiotic ointment with its original label.

hydrocortisone-cream.definition: A topical corticosteroid medicine used for certain inflammatory or itchy skin conditions under appropriate label or professional guidance.
hydrocortisone-cream.exampleUsage: Hydrocortisone cream was kept in its labeled packaging.

stretcher.definition: A flat support used to carry a person who cannot walk safely.
stretcher.exampleUsage: The trainer shows an empty stretcher used to carry a person lying down.

wheelchair.definition: A movable chair mounted on large wheels.

crutch.definition: A support held under the arm or around the forearm to help someone walk.

splint.definition: A firm support used to keep an injured body part still.

neck-brace.definition: A supportive device worn around the neck to restrict movement.
neck-brace.exampleUsage: A neck brace is on the equipment shelf.

ice-pack.definition: A container of ice or cold gel used to cool a part of the body.
ice-pack.exampleUsage: The trainer shows a sealed ice pack.

hot-pack.definition: A pack designed to provide controlled heat for temporary therapeutic use.
hot-pack.exampleUsage: The first-aid room stores hot packs for supervised use.

stethoscope.definition: A medical instrument for listening to the sounds generated inside the body.
stethoscope.exampleUsage: The stethoscope and thermometer are beside it.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The stethoscope and thermometer are beside it.

pulse-oximeter.definition: A small noninvasive device that estimates blood oxygen saturation and pulse rate, usually by clipping onto a fingertip.
pulse-oximeter.exampleUsage: The nurse used a pulse oximeter as part of an assessment.

eye-wash-station.definition: An emergency fixture that provides a flow of clean water or approved solution for rinsing the eyes after certain exposures.
eye-wash-station.exampleUsage: The safety tour identified the eye-wash station location.

cpr-mask.definition: A barrier device used by trained responders during rescue breathing to reduce direct contact.
cpr-mask.exampleUsage: The first-aid cabinet contained a sealed CPR mask.

aed.definition: An automated external defibrillator, a device that analyzes heart rhythm and can deliver a shock when its built-in system determines one is needed.
aed.exampleUsage: The AED is emergency equipment intended to be used according to its prompts and trained-response procedures.

first-aid-manual.definition: A reference book that explains recognized first-aid principles and emergency-response guidance.
first-aid-manual.exampleUsage: The room keeps a current first-aid manual for trained staff.

blood-glucose-monitor.definition: A device that measures the amount of glucose in a blood sample or, in some systems, estimates glucose through a sensor.
blood-glucose-monitor.exampleUsage: A healthcare professional checked the blood-glucose monitor.

blood-pressure-cuff.definition: An inflatable cuff used with a blood-pressure measuring device to help determine arterial blood pressure.
blood-pressure-cuff.exampleUsage: The nurse wrapped the blood-pressure cuff around the patient's upper arm.

penlight.definition: A small flashlight resembling a fountain pen.

tongue-depressor.definition: A small flat tool used by a clinician to hold the tongue down during an examination.

plaster.definition: A small adhesive dressing for a minor skin wound; this is the British English medical sense.
plaster.exampleUsage: The small plaster is still in its wrapper.

butterfly-strip.definition: A narrow adhesive wound-closure strip shaped to pull the edges of a small cut together.
butterfly-strip.exampleUsage: Butterfly strips were kept in the first-aid supply drawer.

wound-dressing.definition: A sterile or clean covering placed over a wound to protect it and manage fluid.
wound-dressing.exampleUsage: The first-aid cabinet contained several sizes of wound dressing.

saline-solution.definition: A solution of salt in water, prepared for a particular medical use.
saline-solution.exampleUsage: The trainer shows a sealed container of saline solution.

hydrogen-peroxide.definition: This clear liquid compound, usually dissolved in water, is used to disinfect, bleach, and oxidize materials.

iodine.definition: A chemical element needed to make thyroid hormones; some antiseptic preparations contain iodine.
iodine.exampleUsage: The instructor explains that iodine is an element, not the name of every antiseptic.

cotton-swab.definition: A small stick with cotton at each end, used for careful cleaning or applying products.

sterile-gloves.definition: Disposable gloves processed to be free of viable microorganisms and used for procedures requiring sterile technique.
sterile-gloves.exampleUsage: Sterile gloves were stored in sealed packages.

syringe.definition: A medical instrument used to inject or withdraw fluids.
syringe.exampleUsage: The sterile gloves and syringe remain in their packets.

suture-kit.definition: A set of sterile instruments and materials intended for wound suturing by trained healthcare professionals.
suture-kit.exampleUsage: The suture kit is reserved for qualified healthcare professionals.

wound-closure-strip.definition: An adhesive strip designed to hold the edges of some small wounds together.
wound-closure-strip.exampleUsage: The first-aid supplies included sterile wound-closure strips.

skin-stapler.definition: A medical device used by trained healthcare professionals to close certain surgical or traumatic wounds with sterile staples.
skin-stapler.exampleUsage: The skin stapler is used only by qualified medical personnel.

wound-irrigation-syringe.definition: A syringe designed to direct cleaning fluid toward a wound during clinical wound care by trained personnel.
wound-irrigation-syringe.exampleUsage: The irrigation syringe was stored with professional wound-care supplies.

rubbing-alcohol.definition: A poisonous liquid made with isopropyl alcohol or denatured ethanol for use on the skin.

burn-gel.definition: A gel product labeled for cooling or covering certain minor burns; significant burns need professional medical assessment.
burn-gel.exampleUsage: The first-aid cabinet contained packaged burn gel.

iodine-solution.definition: A liquid antiseptic preparation containing iodine, used for selected skin-cleaning purposes according to its label or clinical guidance.
iodine-solution.exampleUsage: The iodine solution remained in its labeled container.

defibrillator.definition: A device that gives an electric shock to help restore a normal heart rhythm.
defibrillator.exampleUsage: The trainer names an AED, short for automated external defibrillator.

oxygen-mask.definition: A mask worn over the nose and mouth to supply oxygen from connected equipment.
oxygen-mask.exampleUsage: The defibrillator and oxygen mask are on another shelf.

oxygen-tank.definition: A high-pressure cylinder containing medical oxygen for use by appropriately trained or authorized people.
oxygen-tank.exampleUsage: The medical oxygen tank was secured and handled by trained staff.

epipen.definition: A brand of epinephrine auto-injector prescribed for emergency treatment of severe allergic reactions.
epipen.exampleUsage: The emergency plan states that prescribed epinephrine auto-injectors are used according to medical guidance and device instructions.

tourniquet.definition: A device tightened around a limb to control severe bleeding.
tourniquet.exampleUsage: The instructor identifies a tourniquet in the training equipment.

emergency-blanket.definition: A lightweight insulating blanket designed to reduce heat loss in an emergency.
emergency-blanket.exampleUsage: The first-aid bag included a folded emergency blanket.

whistle.definition: A small object blown to make a loud signal.

emergency-phone.definition: A telephone provided for urgent calls.

alarm-button.definition: A button that activates an emergency alert or calls for assistance.
alarm-button.exampleUsage: The alarm button is clearly marked near the door.

inhaler.definition: A device that delivers medicine for a person to breathe into the airways.
inhaler.exampleUsage: The instructor names an inhaler during the equipment tour.

cervical-collar.definition: A rigid or semi-rigid medical support used by trained responders to restrict movement of the neck when appropriate.
cervical-collar.exampleUsage: The cervical collar was stored with emergency equipment.

spine-board.definition: A rigid board used by trained emergency personnel for selected patient-moving or immobilization situations.
spine-board.exampleUsage: The spine board is emergency equipment for trained responders.

snakebite-kit.definition: A commercially sold emergency kit marketed for snakebite situations; many kit components are not recommended, and suspected venomous bites require urgent professional medical care.
snakebite-kit.exampleUsage: The safety poster says suspected venomous snakebite requires urgent emergency medical care rather than relying on a kit.

tick-remover.definition: A small tool designed to help remove an attached tick from the skin.
tick-remover.exampleUsage: The first-aid cabinet included a purpose-made tick remover.

medical-id-bracelet.definition: A bracelet displaying important medical information that emergency responders may need to know.
medical-id-bracelet.exampleUsage: The medical ID bracelet listed an important health alert.

examination-table.definition: A padded table designed to support a person during a medical examination.
examination-table.exampleUsage: The patient sat on the examination table.

sink.definition: A bowl with taps and a drain, used for washing your hands or face.

soap-dispenser.definition: A device that dispenses liquid soap when its pump or sensor is activated.
soap-dispenser.exampleUsage: The sink and soap dispenser are across the room.

waste-bin.definition: A container used for ordinary waste; medical facilities use separate approved containers for hazardous or clinical waste.
waste-bin.exampleUsage: The room has clearly labeled waste bins.

medicine-cabinet.definition: A cupboard used to store medicines and basic health supplies.

wall-chart.definition: A large chart displayed on a wall to present reference information or instructions.
wall-chart.exampleUsage: The wall chart summarizes emergency contact information.

hand-sanitizer.definition: A liquid or gel used to clean your hands when soap and water are unavailable.

privacy-screen.definition: A movable screen used to give a patient visual privacy during care.
privacy-screen.exampleUsage: The nurse closed the privacy screen.

emergency-contact-card.definition: A card listing people or services to contact in an emergency.
emergency-contact-card.exampleUsage: The emergency-contact card was kept near the telephone.

incident-report-form.definition: A form used to record facts about an accident, injury, safety event, or other incident.
incident-report-form.exampleUsage: The staff member completed an incident-report form after the event.

poison-control-poster.definition: A poster giving safety information and contact details for poison-control or emergency toxicology services.
poison-control-poster.exampleUsage: The poison-control poster was displayed beside the emergency phone.

cpr-poster.definition: A reference poster summarizing recognized CPR emergency-response guidance for trained or supervised use.
cpr-poster.exampleUsage: A current CPR poster was displayed with other emergency information.

fire-extinguisher.definition: A portable or fixed device that releases a suitable substance to put out or contain a small fire.
fire-extinguisher.exampleUsage: The CPR poster and fire extinguisher are separate items.

sharps-container.definition: A puncture-resistant approved container used for disposing of needles and other sharp medical items.
sharps-container.exampleUsage: Used sharps are placed in an approved sharps container by trained staff.

cut.definition: An opening or injury in the skin made by something sharp.
cut.exampleUsage: The trainer explains the word cut in a written example.

bruise.definition: An injury that doesn't break the skin but results in some discoloration.

burn.definition: An injury to skin or tissue caused by heat, chemicals, electricity, or radiation.

sprain.definition: An injury caused by stretching or tearing the ligaments around a joint.

fracture.definition: A crack or break in a bone.

nosebleed.definition: Bleeding from the inside of the nose.

bee-sting.definition: An injury caused by a bee's stinger.

rash.definition: An area of irritated or inflamed skin that may have bumps, spots, itching, or a change in color.
rash.exampleUsage: The instructor explains the word rash during a vocabulary class.

blister.definition: A small raised area on the skin containing fluid.
blister.exampleUsage: The trainer explains the word blister without asking learners to diagnose an injury.

splinter.definition: A small thin sharp bit of wood or glass or metal.

concussion.definition: A brain injury caused by a blow or jolt to the head or body.

dislocation.definition: An injury in which a bone is forced out of its normal position at a joint.

choking.definition: Blocked airflow caused by an object or food lodged in the airway.

allergic-reaction.definition: An immune response to a substance that the body treats as harmful.
allergic-reaction.exampleUsage: The class reads the phrase allergic reaction in a training example.

heat-stroke.definition: A life-threatening condition in which the body overheats and cannot regulate its temperature normally, requiring urgent emergency medical care.
heat-stroke.exampleUsage: Suspected heat stroke is a medical emergency requiring immediate professional help.

hypothermia.definition: A dangerous drop in body temperature caused by exposure to cold.

tape.definition: A strip of sticky material used to attach things.

antiseptic.definition: A substance used on living tissue to reduce harmful microorganisms.

sling.definition: Bandage to support an injured forearm.

compress.definition: A cloth or pad applied to a part of the body, often warm or cold.

gloves.definition: Handwear: covers the hand and wrist.

cpr.definition: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: an emergency procedure involving chest compressions, with rescue breaths when appropriate, after cardiac arrest.
cpr.exampleUsage: The instructor explains what the initials CPR stand for.

wound-care.definition: The assessment and care of wounds by appropriately trained people.

check-pulse.definition: To assess whether a pulse or heartbeat can be detected as part of a medical or emergency assessment.
check-pulse.exampleUsage: A trained responder may check a pulse during an assessment.

apply-pressure.definition: To press firmly against something; the precise medical action depends on professional guidance.
apply-pressure.exampleUsage: Omar asks the instructor what apply pressure means.

elevate.definition: To raise something to a higher position.
elevate.exampleUsage: The instructor explains that elevate means raise something.

immobilize.definition: To keep a body part from moving by providing support or a restraint.

call-emergency.definition: To contact the local emergency-services number or emergency response system for urgent professional help.
call-emergency.exampleUsage: The safety plan says to call emergency services for a life-threatening situation.

monitor.definition: To observe or check something over a period of time; this lesson teaches the verb.
monitor.exampleUsage: The instructor explains the verb monitor in a vocabulary class.

paper-towel.definition: A sheet of absorbent paper used for drying or wiping.
paper-towel.exampleUsage: Omar takes a paper towel from the dispenser above the sink.
